insight.title: Why Adding More People Makes Projects Slower
insight.subtitle: Why extra help often creates more delays than it solves

sections.text: City planners often find that closing a major road actually improves traffic flow. In business strategy, we assume the opposite: that adding more resources or "roads" will always get us to the goal faster.

This is because new options change how people behave. Adding a new person or tool creates additional layers of communication and decision-making, which can paradoxically slow the entire system down to a crawl.

Complexity scales faster than productivity. When a project stalls, the instinct to add more help usually backfires. The most effective strategy is often to remove a step or limit the number of participants.
Try this today: When you invite someone to a meeting today, ask if their presence simplifies the decision.
The most efficient systems are usually the ones with the fewest moving parts.
